description.value: This study examined neocortical brain morphometric differences between abstinent polysubstance dependent and alcohol-only dependent treatment seekers and light drinking controls, associations of cigarette smoking in polysubstance users, and morphometric relationships to cognition and inhibitory control.

spans.text: This study examined neocortical brain morphometric differences between abstinent polysubstance dependent and alcohol-only dependent treatment seekers (ALC) as well as light drinking controls (CON), the associations of cigarette smoking in these polysubstance users (PSU), and morphometric relationships to cognition and inhibitory control.

value: we posited that one-month abstinent PSU exhibit abnormal morphometry in these neocortical regions, namely smaller cortical volumes, surface areas and thinner cortices than CON and—more informatively—compared to an age- and abstinence duration-matched cohort of ALC.
We further hypothesized that smoking PSU have smaller cortical volumes, surface areas and thinner cortices in these frontal regions than non-smoking PSU.

description.value: Cross-sectional observational study of treatment-seeking polysubstance-dependent and alcohol-dependent participants and light-drinking controls; all participants were male and assessed after approximately one month of abstinence for PSU and ALC.

spans.text: One hundred and thirty-three male volunteers participated in study procedures.
